title: A Personal Word to Baruch
overview: God answers the despair of Baruch, Jeremiah's assistant, by telling him not to chase big things while the nation falls, but promising he will come through alive.

parts.label: When this was said (v. 1)
parts.note: This message is dated to the fourth year of King Jehoiakim, around 605 BC, when Baruch, Jeremiah's scribe, was writing Jeremiah's messages onto a scroll, as chapter 36 describes. It was probably placed near the end of the book because it is a private word to one person rather than to the nation.

parts.label: Baruch's complaint (vv. 2-3)
parts.note: Baruch cries that the LORD has piled sorrow on top of his pain, and that he is worn out with groaning and can find no rest. Writing down warnings of his own country's ruin was grim work that also put him at risk, though scholars are unsure exactly which troubles he had in mind.

parts.label: The bigger picture (v. 4)
parts.note: God says he is tearing down the nation he once built and pulling up what he once planted, like a gardener uprooting his own vineyard. Baruch's troubles are set inside a much larger collapse.

parts.label: Don't seek great things (v. 5)
parts.note: Baruch is told not to look for great things for himself while everything around him is being lost, though it is unclear whether he hoped for a career, for standing, or simply for an easier road. What he is promised is his life, kept like plunder grabbed when a city falls, wherever he goes.

think: Would it feel like a relief or a loss to be told that simply getting through a hard season with your life is enough?
